NEW DELHI: BJP lodged a complaint with the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Hyderabad "provocative" political remarks made by foreign political representatives at the Bharat Summit held in Hyderabad.The complaint comes amid a political row over Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck's participation in the Congress-organised Bharat Summit 2026, where he had called for international support for the opposition.Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao submitted the complaint on Monday to the FRRO in Shamshabad, accusing foreign political representatives of interfering in India's internal affairs through their comments at the summit.Speaking to ANI on Monday, Rao described the event as an "anti-Bharat Summit" and said Filibeck's remarks had vindicated the BJP's concerns about the gathering."As BJP was maintaining, it is not a Bharat Summit; it is an anti-Bharat Summit. Our apprehensions have proved correct, with an Italian politician interfering in India's internal affairs. Any foreign national visiting another country must respect and abide by that country's laws and regulations," he said.
Rao also criticised Rahul Gandhi for applauding Filibeck's comments and said the BJP had sought action through its memorandum to the FRRO."Unfortunately, while the Italian politician was commenting on our Prime Minister, Rahul Gandhi was seen applauding. The BJP condemns this and will meet the Chief of FRRO today to submit a memorandum, seeking action against those involved...," he added.Filibeck, secretary general of the Party of European Socialists (PES), had said on Saturday that democracy was "under attack" in India and called for international support for the Congress.He also used the slogan "Vote Chor Gaddi Chhod," a Hindi political slogan that translates as “those who stole the vote must vacate their seats”."I believe that this kind of gatherings, conference, summit are vital to raise international attention on concerning challenges. The remarks also drew criticism in Italy, with Italian legislator Deborah Bergamini questioning Filibeck's intervention in India's domestic political debate. Invoking the special strategic partnership between India and Italy, she said foreign representatives should not lecture a friendly country on democracy.“Moreover, as Europeans, we find it inappropriate to lecture on democracy a nation that enables 970 million citizens to cast their votes. Thousands run Cuba’s Marabana marathon as many protest US sanctions
Thousands of people have run in Cuba’s Marabana marathon, using the event to protest U.S. economic sanctions
HAVANA -- Thousands of people ran Sunday in Cuba’s most important international marathon, with some using the race to protest U.S. economic sanctions against the island.
The Marabana marathon, held every November to commemorate the founding of Havana, took runners along city's iconic streets and landmarks, such as the Paseo del Prado and the Capitol building. Many wore signs expressing solidarity with Cuba.
“Cuba is not a threat; the blockade is,” read the signs that many of the 3,000 participants wore on their backs.
The U.S. embargo against Cuba was first imposed in 1960, after Fidel Castro led a revolution that toppled dictator Fulgencio Batista and nationalized properties belonging to U.S. citizens and corporations. As a result, the Caribbean country has endured decades of economic and financial troubles and is now being pushed to a breaking point after U.S. President Donald Trump announced in late January that he would impose tariffs on any country that sells or provides oil to Cuba.
The warning has effectively cut off fuel to the island, leading to widespread power outages that disrupt water supplies and internet and telephone services.
“The blockade is suffocating the Cuban people," Yuraldi Cava, a 58-year-old state employee, said while running. “We are going to win this fight.”
Mayté Vigoa, Havana’s provincial government coordinator for sports, said the city had to make a major effort to hold the international race because of the island’s precarious economic conditions. She confirmed that the sportswear brand Adidas, a longtime sponsor of the competition, did not provide support this year.
Other companies with longstanding ties to Cuba, including Meliá Hotels International, said they were withdrawing from the island because of the tightening of sanctions.
Participants included families with children and people with disabilities dressed in sportswear and carrying water bottles as enthusiastic onlookers cheered them on from the sidewalks.
Those protesting the sanctions included foreigners who wore red-and-white sweatshirts with the message “Cuba is not alone.”
The marathon is recognized by the Association of International Marathons and Distance Races, and runners can use their times as official qualifying marks. The event also features a half-marathon, as well as the more popular 10-kilometer and 5-kilometer races.

Shinji Saito, a former member of the popular Japanese comedy group Jungle Pocket, was sentenced to four years in prison by the Tokyo District Court on Monday for sexually assaulting a female co-star on a television production bus.
Saito, 44, was convicted of forcible sexual intercourse and indecent assault for groping a woman in her 20s and forcing her to perform oral sex while the two were alone on the bus between filming in Tokyo’s Shinjuku Ward in July 2024. He was a member of Jungle Pocket until Yoshimoto Kogyo, the comedy group’s agency, terminated his contract following his referral to prosecutors in October 2024.
The case hinged on whether the acts were consensual. Saito admitted to the acts but pleaded not guilty, claiming that the woman, a company employee who also worked as an influencer, had appeared to enjoy the encounter and kissed him back at the end. The defense also argued that he had no influence over her career.
The prosecution countered that the woman had resisted Saito’s advances but was unable to do so fully because he was in a position to influence the woman’s employment, despite the fact that they had met for the first time that day.
The court accepted the prosecution’s argument, finding that a power imbalance existed between the two and that this helped explain why the woman had difficulty resisting his advances and reporting the incident.
“It is hard to imagine that the defendant, without checking with the victim, could have believed that the victim was consenting to sexual acts, or failed to realize that the victim was in a situation where it was difficult for her to refuse to consent,” said Judge Yuko Ito in the court’s ruling.
The court also found that the woman’s statements were backed up by the fact that she had told her mother and an acquaintance about how she felt uncomfortable about the encounter and visited a psychiatrist to discuss it, and said that Saito was fully responsible for the crimes.
“There are no other motives behind the defendant’s crimes other than satisfying his own sexual desires without any consideration for others,” said Ito, adding that Saito made “illogical justifications” for his actions and did not express remorse.
Jungle Pocket was formed in 2006 by Saito along with comedians Hirohisa Ota and Otake, and they specialized in conte, a style of skit-based comedy. The group competed in a variety of comedy programs, including a second-place finish in the 2016 edition of TBS’ annual “King of Conte” comedy competition.

A video is being shared on social media (here, here, and here) with the claim that it shows Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat saying that those who call India a Hindu nation should be sent to a mental hospital. Let’s verify the truth behind the video in this article.
Claim: The video shows RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat saying that those who call India a Hindu nation should be sent to a mental hospital.
Fact: The video is clipped out of context. RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat was recounting an incident from the 1930s where a person named Ibrahim defended the RSS against an attempt to ban it. While making this argument, Ibrahim had said that those who call India a Hindu nation should be sent to a mental asylum. Bhagwat was quoting Ibrahim’s statement, not remarking himself. Hence, the claim made in the post is FALSE.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a Facebook post (archived) by The Economic Times, dated 09 November 2026, featuring a longer version of the same video. Upon reviewing the video, we found that Mohan Bhagwat was not making the statement himself but was quoting a person named Ibrahim. Referring to an incident from the 1930s, Bhagwat said that when the Central Provinces Assembly first attempted to ban the RSS, there were no volunteers or supporters of the RSS’s ideology to defend it. In this context, he recounted that a person named Ibrahim defended the RSS by saying that those who call India a Hindu nation should be sent to a mental asylum. Ibrahim further stated that he knew Dr Hedgewar, that he was not insane but a good man, and therefore, the RSS could not be communal.
We also found multiple media reports (here, here, and here) covering the statement made by Mohan Bhagwat on 09 November 2026, while inaugurating the newly constructed auditorium at the renovated headquarters of Nagpur Nagarik Sahakari Bank Limited in Nagpur.
We also found a video of the event, which was livestreamed on 09 November 2026 on the Facebook account of Nagpur Nagarik Sahakari Bank Ltd. In the approximately 1-hour-and-36-minute-long video, we found the segment corresponding to the viral clip at around 1:16:00.
During this segment, Mohan Bhagwat said, “The RSS, which was formed 100 years ago, is being discussed everywhere. That’s why so many books are being published now. I held an intellectual class here in Nagpur, where I explained that when the first attempt to ban the RSS was made in the Central Provinces Assembly in the 1930s, none of the RSS volunteers came forward to defend the RSS or support its ideology.”
He further said, “There was a Mr Ibrahim who spoke in favour of the RSS. He said that the RSS should not be banned and that it was not communal. But how did he make this argument? He said that those who say India is a Hindu nation should be sent to a mental asylum. This is my opinion, and I know Dr Hedgewar. He is not insane; he is a good man, and therefore, the RSS cannot be communal. So, that was in the 1930s. Five or seven years had passed since the RSS was founded. Everyone knew about the RSS, but Dr Hedgewar knew“
We also found that Jagran reported that a book on the lives of former RSS pracharaks was released during the event. Bhagwat discussed the lives of former RSS pracharaks and recounted an incident from the 1930s in this context. This confirms that the viral clip presents Bhagwat’s statement without the necessary context. In the original video, Bhagwat was quoting a person named Ibrahim, who had said that those who call India a Hindu nation should be sent to a mental asylum. The remark was made by Ibrahim, not Bhagwat.
To sum up, this video shows Mohan Bhagwat quoting Ibrahim’s remark about sending those who call India a Hindu nation to a mental asylum.

A California man who killed a father of five showed zero remorse at his sentencing hearing, telling the victim’s family, “I’d do it a million times.”
William Carney, 39, was fatally shot at a gas station in Fresno in October 2023, and weeks later, Damien Murphy was arrested for his murder.
Murphy was sentenced to 32 years in prison Thursday after pleading no contest to voluntary manslaughter in September to avoid a first-degree murder conviction and a longer sentence, according to local reports.
"I hope every second of your 32 years, you think about William and his family and the damage you've caused," said the judge presiding over the hearing, according to local outlet KFSN.
The judge then gave Murphy a chance to address the court, but he refused to apologize to Carney’s family.
"I would apologize, but I'm not going to apologize for protecting my family. I'd do it a million times," he said.
It’s unclear what exactly led to the fatal shooting, but it was supposedly linked to a confrontation between the victim and Murphy’s family, local outlet KMPH reported in November 2023.
"I hope you change your mind and have some remorse for your actions, and don't be disrespectful to the people you murdered and hurt their families," the judge said in response to Murphy’s chilling confession.
Heartbroken members of Carney’s family spoke at Thursday’s hearing about his death, which they said happened less than a month before his 40th birthday.
"It was like all my dreams died at once," Carney’s daughter told the court. "My dad won't ever see me on prom day. He can never walk me down the aisle on my wedding day and cry, seeing how much I've grown.”
Carney’s mother said her life “simply no longer holds the happiness it once had. The joy that used to come naturally has been replaced by grief."
"I can't hate you because I know you're suffering more than he is, and that brings me peace of mind," one of Carney’s childhood friends told Murphy.

Tolu Arokodare was the hero as Nigeria boosted their hopes of reaching the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) with a 3-1 home win over tournament co-hosts Tanzania.
With the East Africans already assured of a spot at the finals, the Super Eagles are battling for the one qualification spot available in Group L and have little margin for error after losing 3-0 in Guinea-Bissau in September.
Alhassan Yusuf kept his composure to slot Nigeria into a second-minute lead in Uyo from Ademola Lookman's pass, but the visitors equalised through Alphonce Msanga just after the half-hour mark.
Arokodare climbed off the bench at half-time and cleverly flicked home Wilfred Ndidi's low ball to restore the lead for the West Africans in the 52nd minute.
And the Ajax striker, who is on a season-long loan from Wolves, gave the Super Eagles breathing space eight minutes later when he controlled Moses Usor's cross from the left and smashed in from 12 yards out.
With three games played in the group, Eric Chelle's side are now one point behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who drew 1-1 with Madagascar on Thursday.

Elsewhere, Mohamed Salah scored twice late on against Malawi as Egypt cruised to a 5-0 victory in Ali Maher's first match in charge.
Achraf Hakimi netted two stunning goals and Yassine Bounou saved a penalty to help Morocco continue their unbeaten start with a 5-1 win over Niger.
Meanwhile, Tunisia are in danger of missing out on the finals for the first time since 1992 after suffering a 2-0 defeat at home against Libya, and Kenya scored a last-minute equaliser to end South Africa's perfect start.
The third round of qualifying culminates with three games on Saturday, while the fourth round of fixtures are split across Monday and Tuesday.
Salah and Hakimi shine
Egypt reached the semi-finals of Afcon 2025 and the last 16 of this year's Fifa World Cup under Hossam Hassan but parted company with the 60-year-old earlier this month.
The Pharaohs had taken four points from their opening two games in Group B, with Salah substituted after an hour in their 0-0 draw with Angola before missing the win in South Sudan.
The former Liverpool forward returned as captain against Malawi, and Egypt cruised into a 3-0 lead at the break through goals from Nasser Maher, Omar Marmoush and Mohamed Hany.
Salah got on the scoresheet when he stooped to head in a cross from the left and rounded off proceedings by dinking in a penalty after Hamza Abdelkarim was tripped in the box.
Victory in Maher's first game at the helm puts Egypt three points clear of Angola, who take on South Sudan on Saturday.
In Group A, Morocco had also looked like they would ease to three points against Niger in Casablanca after Yassir Zabiri's early effort and a brilliant long-range strike from right-back Hakimi put them 2-0 up after 27 minutes.
But Mohamed Abdourahmane headed in to halve the deficit and Niger had a chance to level from the spot on the stroke of half-time after a handball by Noussair Mazraoui.
However, Atlas Lions goalkeeper Bounou moved to his left to keep out Youssouf Oumarou's penalty, and Hakimi made it 3-1 in first-half stoppage time with a dipping free-kick from distance.
Youssef En-Nesyri steered in the fourth in the 77th minute from a Hakimi pass and Ayoub Oufkir completed the scoring from close range in the final minute.
Earlier in Group A on Friday Gabon beat Lesotho to move on to six points thanks to two second-half goals from Denis Bouanga.

Tunisia have appeared at a record 17 consecutive Afcons but are winless and bottom of Group H - another section with just one qualifying place on offer - after defeat by their North African neighbours Libya.
The Carthage Eagles could complain about refereeing decisions going against them in Sfax, with Ali Maaloul penalised for a shirt pull on Muad Eisay just before half-time and Ali Youssef converting the resulting spot-kick.
Tunisia had a goal ruled out following a marginal offside call in the second half and three minutes later a low shot from Hamdou El Houni made it 2-0 to the Mediterranean Knights.
Libya, who last played at an Afcon in 2012, climb to second in the table and go level on points with Uganda.
South Africa are a point clear of Guinea at the top of Group D after a 2-2 draw against Benni McCarthy's Kenya in Johannesburg.
Amos Wanjala's own goal gifted the hosts an early lead before Michael Olunga levelled from the penalty spot just before half-time.
Relebohile Mofokeng restored Bafana Bafana's advantage with 13 minutes remaining, but Kenya claimed a point when Ryan Ogam's low shot from 20 yards crept inside the left-hand upright in the 90th minute.
Elsewhere, Burkina Faso joined Benin on seven points at the top of Group F thanks to Elohim Kabore's 94th-minute winner against Mauritania in Ouagadougou.
Ethiopia upset Mozambique
Mali extended their winning start to go top of Group K after Mamadou Camara completed a 3-2 comeback win at home against Rwanda, who had led twice in Bamako.
Rwanda had won their first two fixtures and are three points ahead of Cape Verde, who registered their first points with a 4-2 victory over Liberia in Praia.
Ethiopia registered their first win to upset Mozambique in Maputo, with Kenean Markneh scoring the only goal in the 87th minute after Mambas keeper Ernan spilled a low shot from Carlos Damtew.
The East Africans move on to three points but remain bottom of Group J, behind Sudan on head-to-head record, while Mozambique are on four points and three behind leaders Senegal.
Zambia moved level on four points with Group I leaders Algeria after a 1-1 draw at home to Burundi. The North Africans have the chance to open up a three-point gap when they host Togo on Saturday.
In Group G, Comoros were held to a goalless draw by Congo-Brazzaville in Moroni. Cameroon lead the section on seven points, with Comoros on four, Namibia on three and the Congolese bottom on two points.

At least 17 people were killed in two separate shootings in South Africa over the weekend, police have confirmed.
Nine people, including three women, were found dead with gunshot wounds inside a shack in the informal settlement of Jeffsville, located near the capital of Pretoria.
Eight others were found dead inside a vehicle in Sweetwaters outside the city of Pietermaritzburg, located near the coastal city of Durban.
Police have not yet established a motive for either of the killings.
The shooting in Jeffsville is reported to have taken place on Sunday night but no arrests have been made. In Pietermaritzburg, police said they had not yet identified the victims.
South Africa has one of the highest murder rates in the world, averaging about 60 every day.
While there is no standard global definition of mass shooting, in South Africa police define a mass shooting as when three or more people are shot in a single attack.
The country also has high rates of gun crime, including shootings related to local political rivalries.
Authorities say that many of the mass shootings are linked to criminal gangs fighting turf wars or using violence to establish control over communities and areas. The mass killings also tend to happen in the country’s poorest communities
A report from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime found that there had been 43 killings in South Africa this year that were suspected to be politically motivated.
In September, at least 17 people were killed in a mass shooting at a bar in Gauteng. All of the victims, including four women, were declared dead at the scene by the ambulance service.
Last month, at least two people were killed after a gunman opened fire at a memorial service in Katlehong township, located southeast of Johannesburg.
The two victims were members of the youth league of the African National Congress (ANC) party, the largest party in South Africa’s Parliament which describes itself as a “disciplined force of the left”.
The suspected gunman turned himself in while the South African Police Service said that the shooting was being investigated by a political killings task team.

Mirra Andreeva beats Elina Svitolina as she storms to WTA Finals title without dropping a set: 'It's something unbelievable'
Mirra Andreeva defeated Elina Svitolina 7-5 6-3 to win the WTA Finals; They were playing each other for the second time in the tournament after Andreeva's dominant win over Svitolina in the group stage; Svitolina was far more competitive in the final but could not derail the teenager
Monday 16 November 2026 00:01, UK
Mirra Andreeva concluded a stunning week with a second victory over Elina Svitolina to claim the WTA Finals title.
The Russian teenager, who laughed off being called a diva by rival Jessica Pegula in a 'hot mic' moment ahead of the tournament, did not drop a set on her singles debut at the season-ending showpiece, finishing with a 7-5 6-3 success.
At 19, the French Open champion is the first woman to claim the title before her 20th birthday since compatriot Maria Sharapova 22 years ago.
Andreeva had conceded only 18 games on route to the final, the fewest since the reintroduction of the round-robin format in 2003, with four of those coming in a dominant group win over Ukrainian Svitolina.
Their rematch in the final was much more competitive, with the pair, who are two of the best athletes in the sport, engaging in lengthy, lung-busting exchanges in intense rallies.
But Svitolina just could not get her nose in front and Andreeva finally served out the opening set at the second time of asking.
Svitolina, who won the title back in 2018, was grimly determined to hang on in the second set but Andreeva was strong, quick and unrelenting. The teenager jumped in the air with delight when Svitolina blasted an overarm smash into the net to concede the second match point.
Andreeva became the 11th player to win the Finals without losing a set, joining among others Chris Evert, Martina Navratilova and Serena Williams.
Andreeva, who will climb to second in the world rankings on Monday, told Sky Sports: "Coming into this match, it was the second time in my life that I thought I'm just going to die on the court but she's not getting the win.
"I'm going to have blisters, I'm going to have cramps, I'm going to have everything that you possibly can have, but I'm not going to lose this match.
"This spirit, this fighting mindset, just helped me to get through, helped me to get more brave and more aggressive in the important moments. It's crazy, something unbelievable. I'm so, so happy."

At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.
Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.
Roots in fitness routine of vicar
The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.
“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.
When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.
“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.
The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.
The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.
“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.
For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.
‘A form of spiritual service’
The church sees the initiative as more than a fitness facility. “We want to groom a healthy generation. Many people suffer from lifestyle diseases, while youngsters often turn to private fitness centres. We felt that providing basic facilities here would benefit the community. Spirituality is also about nurturing a healthy mind and body. We consider this a form of spiritual service,” says assistant vicar Fr. Jees Akkara.
For Fr. Eluvathingal, there is another purpose. “Youngsters rarely come to church or participate in its activities these days. This is also an opportunity to bring more of them into the church community,” he says.

Triumph or flop? The Rugby League World Cup that split opinion
- Published
Has the 2026 Rugby League World Cup been a success or not?
It depends on who you listen to - and perhaps where in the world you are.
The men's, women's and wheelchair tournaments provided plenty of stories - from Kalyn Ponga's return from a broken arm in 23 days, to Jodie Cunningham's mangled ear,, external to the England wheelchair team's golden ladder, to the men's group format that caused widespread bafflement.
But was the World Cup a triumph? The northern and southern hemisphere perspectives provide contrasting answers.
For the fourth tournament running, Australia won the men's and women's titles, with New Zealand unable to deliver a twist in either final.
Tonga and Samoa brought vibrancy and passion - performing to a level that underlined why they are being elevated to Tier One status. The large Polynesian population in the USA - which will co-host the 2030 men's and women's World Cups - is likely to be key in spreading the rugby league word further around the world.
England's Wheelchair World Cup win, in a thunderous final against their old foes France, offset some of the disappointment felt when Brian McDermott's men and Stuart Barrow's women went home early.
And unlike when the game was emerging from post-pandemic constraints in 2022, the tournament has also worked financially by posting a profit.
"This whole tournament's been incredible," said Australia men's captain Isaah Yeo.
"Not just the fans here for New Zealand and Australia, but just everyone. I thought it was all outstanding.
"I think it's to date the most competitive and the best World Cup there's been. I think that's only going to continue to grow."
That sentiment has been endorsed repeatedly by Australian television broadcaster Channel Seven, which paid a reported A$12m (£6.1m) for exclusive domestic free-to-air coverage of the men's, women's and wheelchair tournaments.
Not everyone has been able to feel that positivity, though.
The decision to cut the men's tournament from 16 teams to 10 reduced the overall number of matches - and deprived teams such as Jamaica and Greece of a chance to build on the feelgood factor they provided as debutants in 2022.
That decision was made after Australia stepped in to stage the tournament, postponed for a year when scheduled hosts France pulled out for financial reasons.
For those who did get to the party this time, it has not always been an even contest. The disparity between the haves and have-nots has been significant.
While the Jillaroos and Kangaroos players will each receive equal payments of $40,000 (£20,500) for competing, Wales will reportedly spread a total of $15,000 (£7,689) across their women's and wheelchair teams., external
Viewer access to the World Cup has varied too. While Australia had free-to-air live television coverage, fans in the UK only got it for the wheelchair final, shown on BBC iPlayer. For all other games, they needed a Premier Sports subscription, which was also the only way to watch the tournament in North America.
With many matches staged at times when British and American viewers were likely to be in bed, it feels as if a chance to spread the game's gospel has been missed.
Festival feel or competitive balance? Or neither?
Many of the players at this World Cup were Australia-based, as they play club rugby in either the NRL's men's competition or its Women's Premiership.
That helped the International Rugby League - the world governing body - to keep costs down, after it spent a vast sum transporting players from the southern hemisphere to England four years ago.
Paring back the men's competition also helped on the costs front, though another supposed benefit - cutting out the lopsided group-stage scorelines of four years ago - has not been evident.
France and the Cook Islands both conceded more than 180 points in the group stage, while scoring a combined 58.
Former England international Ryan Hall told BBC Radio 5 Live earlier this month that the men's World Cup had suffered for being slimmed down - with Scotland, Ireland, Italy and Wales also missing out.
"I don't think it is a World Cup," Hall said. "The essence of any World Cup in any sport is that it's a festival of the sport.
"Compare it to the football World Cup. Curacao were one of the 48 teams in the World Cup.
"I'm not saying rugby league could get 48 teams in the World Cup because that's not achievable, but [they could] certainly [have] more than 10.
"It's meant to be a festival and showcasing everyone of all levels of different countries who's eligible to play."
A format that contained no quarter-finals came in for widespread criticism from pundits, external before a ball was kicked.
The men's tournament featured one group of four and another of six. But two teams went through from both groups, and not everyone in the six-team pool played each other.
In the words of Castleford Tigers head coach Paul Rowley, the former England hooker: "It's trying to make a square with five sides." England captain George Williams, during the build-up, called the format "weird".
And England turned out to be the major losers. The draw left them with no margin for error as an underprepared and jet-lagged squad faced a dangerous Tonga side first up, and lost 30-12.
And ultimately, McDermott's side paid the price. Of the 26 teams across the three World Cups, only one side won two out of three group games and still failed to make the semi-finals: England's men.

  - Published8 hours ago
- Ruthless Australia win record fourth Women's World Cup 
  - Published11 hours ago
- Sharks, ladders and a four-year plan - how England won World Cup 
  - Published2 days ago
A growing audience?
An October and November tournament brings a different vibe depending on where you are. The last World Cup, in the UK, was staged as the temperatures dropped. This time around, it was held with co-hosts Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea heading towards summer.
Fans have gone to games in T-shirts and shorts instead of thick winter garments - and tellingly, average footfall increased.
That is despite the fact that the capacity 52,000 crowd in Brisbane for finals night was lower than the 67,000 at Old Trafford four years ago.
In 2022, the men's group stage - spanning 24 games - was watched by an average crowd of 9,811, itself down on the 14,345 figure from 2013, when England and Wales played hosts.
This time around, the average crowd rose to 21,360. It probably helped that there were fewer group games. It certainly helped that every Australia match was well attended, and that there was strong backing for New Zealand, Samoa, Tonga and Papua New Guinea, who played twice in their capital Port Moresby.
Lessons have also clearly been learned from 2022's heavily criticised ticket pricing structure.
Instead of adults paying more than £20 to attend matches, it has been a more friendly A$19, which equates to £9.74 per ticket.
But while attendances at this year's tournament are up, there is still work to be done around the women's game.
The sight of more empty seats than supporters in grounds for a number of double-headers is hardly a good look for the organisers or broadcasters.
Jillaroos coach Jess Skinner notably raised the issue after her team defeated Samoa 40-0 in their Pool A opener at the home of Parramatta Eels on 16 October.
That match had followed Samoa's men thrashing France 78-4 - but in a stadium with a capacity of 30,000, many of the recorded 13,174 crowd had dispersed before the women's game got under way, with the stands appearing barely 20% full.
"Let's get around women in sport, right? All women in sport, particularly at this Rugby League World Cup," Skinner said. "We've got a lot of talented women across all the teams and the message would be to stay and support that.
"Something really cool's happening in this generation of sport, with our ladies, and you're going to miss history-making moments at this World Cup, no doubt."
Sadly for Skinner and her peerless team, it was a pattern that was repeated in Sunday's final, with the stands in Brisbane's Suncorp Stadium only filling as kick-off time for the men's game approached.
Northern hemisphere indifference?
Four years ago, the Rugby League World Cup was shown free-to-air in the UK by the BBC, with record-breaking viewing figures.
Almost 30 million people tuned in to watch the five-week extravaganza.
This time, the action has largely been behind a paywall. Premier Sports has shown all the World Cup matches live. The BBC showed the wheelchair final live, plus online highlights of selected games from all three tournaments.
In addition, it provided live radio coverage of all men's matches and some women's games, plus live text commentaries on selected games.
Rights were awarded by the International Rugby League - and not the Rugby Football League. Last month, IRL chair Troy Grant told the iPaper that it made the decision to go with Premier because the BBC did not offer enough money - though no other free-to-air broadcaster made a suitable offer either.
Former England international Jon Wilkin highlighted the issue during a BBC Radio 5 Live discussion at the start of this month, saying: "The World Cup should have been on the BBC.
"There is no doubt in my mind as a public service broadcaster, this had so many reasons to be a slam dunk home run to be free to air on the BBC. It had to be."
In response, a BBC spokesperson said: "We must make difficult choices to deliver the savings required while continuing to serve audiences as effectively as possible."
And therein lies a problem for the sport in the northern hemisphere, where more backing, more financial support and more coverage is needed to reverse the fortunes of the Super League and international teams largely bound to that competition.
The financial gulf to southern hemisphere's elite competitions was laid bare, when the NRL struck a record A$5.3bn (£2.78bn) television deal over seven years in July.
Super League's TV deal with Sky Sports, which expired at the end of 2026, was worth around £21.5m per year.
Even with the pending announcement of a deal to bring NRL investment into Super League, that particular playing field is a long way from being levelled.
And it means that when the next World Cup comes around, Australia can expect to be favourites to win the men's and women's tournaments again.

On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop, halting departures from all US airports. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy announced the ground stop on X, citing a “communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.” Duffy promised updates as more information is known and said FAA staff were troubleshooting the problem.
Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that the ground stop was not prompted by a security threat. “This is a telecommunications outage out of the FAA. Out of an abundance of caution, we have grounded all of the flights,” Mullin said. “There’s no indication as of yet that this is a nefarious attack against us.”
Mullin said the FAA would handle incoming international flights on a case-by-case basis.
This is only the third nationwide ground stop issued by the FAA. The first, and most memorable, came during the attacks of September 11, 2001, when the FAA stopped all civilian departures nationwide and subsequently ordered all airborne aircraft to land. Commercial flights did not take off again until September 13. Flights were also grounded for less than two hours the morning of January 11, 2023, after its Notice to Air Missions system suffered an outage.
Unfortunately for travelers, based on what is known so far, this is likely to be a lengthy ground stop. Airlines have already canceled flights scheduled to leave later Friday, and American Airlines warned that disruptions are expected for the rest of the day. “This is going to take some time,” Mullin said. “Flights are accounted for, and there should be no fear to the public at all.”

Brazil legend Ronaldinho made his comeback aged 46 for Ravenna in their 2-0 win over Forli in an Italian third-tier derby.

In his peak playing years, Ronaldinho was one of the best players in the world - as well as one of the most popular for his joyful demeanour and exuberant skill.

He also played for Paris St-Germain as well as Gremio, Flamengo, Atletico Mineiro and Fluminense in his homeland, plus Mexican side Queretaro.

Two Celebrity Cases Put a Spotlight on British Courts’ Gag Orders
Russell Brand and the TV personality David Walliams both persuaded courts to suppress misconduct allegations against them. Some say the libel laws need to change.
Two recent cases have brought new attention to the ways that British laws can allow the wealthy and powerful to silence their critics.
The first was the rape and sexual assault trial of the comedian Russell Brand. Before his conviction last week, Mr. Brand had obtained an injunction prohibiting another accuser from telling almost anyone — including the police, her family and most doctors — about her claims that he assaulted her. (Mr. Brand has denied her allegations.) That injunction, first revealed by Dan Neidle, a tax lawyer and free-expression activist, apparently remains in force.
In the second instance, two British news organizations were temporarily blocked from reporting allegations of sexual misconduct against David Walliams, a television personality and author of children’s books, before a judge declined to make the injunction permanent. The Guardian newspaper and ITV News, a British broadcaster, published investigations last week into the allegations, which Mr. Walliams denies.
Though both men now face public scrutiny, the revelations of how they used court injunctions — essentially gag orders — to protect their reputations have provoked no shortage of public and political outrage. Judges in other cases have issued “super injunctions,” which prohibit publishing any information even about the injunction itself.
“What will the government do to prevent these abuses of process, and stop the abusive injunctions and super injunctions which stop scrutiny, accountability and the work of the free press?” Nick Timothy, the shadow justice minister, asked in Parliament on Tuesday.
The British government is now “looking at what we can do,” Alex Davies-Jones, the government minister responsible for victims of crime and violence against women and girls, said in response.

On Wednesday, Mississippi’s Senate race was officially called for Democrat Scott Colom, who will become the first Black person to represent the state in the US Senate since Reconstruction, more than 140 years ago. Colom’s win is a stunning, historic upset — and for many Black Democrats, like Rep. Bennie Thompson, it’s been a long time coming.
“A rich message, but a poor campaign”: How Scott Colom beat the odds in Mississippi
Rep. Bennie Thompson on his 50-year fight to see a Black senator from Mississippi.
Thompson, who also won his race last week, has represented Mississippi’s majority-Black Second Congressional District since 1993. Over the years, the 78-year-old lawmaker has frequently invoked the story of his father, who was never able to cast a vote because of racist Jim Crow laws that enforced segregation until the mid-1960s.
I sat down with Thompson for Today, Explained to talk about Colom’s run for Senate, how he won, what it means for Thompson personally.
Below is an excerpt of our conversation, edited for length and clarity. There’s much more in the full podcast, so listen to Today, Explained wherever you get podcasts, including Apple Podcasts, Pandora, and Spotify.
Your dad was never able to cast a vote during his lifetime because of Jim Crow laws. And I wonder, growing up in Mississippi, what did you learn about who was allowed to participate in democracy?
You were a second-class citizen. That means you could go to school, but you couldn’t go to school with the white kids. Or the one swimming pool in town was for white kids, and the Black kids had to swim in the creeks or the ponds around the community. No lifeguard, no anything. My mama and daddy paid taxes, but they weren’t allowed to vote. My uncle fought in World War II; defended democracy all over the world, but when he came back home, he had to ride a segregated train behind the white German prisoners.
Jesus.
So you had the white soldiers, the white German prisoners, and the Black soldiers. And that was the order of the day. It was something that we grew up with.
When you were young, I wonder, did you associate the right to vote with the ability to change things? Like, if we get to cast a ballot, then we get to fix this mess?
The best thing that I can say is I went to Tougaloo College [near Jackson, Mississippi]. And on that college campus, I met Martin Luther King Jr., I met Stokely Carmichael, I met Harry Belafonte, I met Sammy Davis Jr. — all of the major civil rights icons of the day.
That was how we cut our teeth into civil rights and voting rights. The first campaign I worked on was Mrs. Hamer’s campaign for Congress.
Fannie Lou Hamer, the civil rights icon.
And I now represent that district.
But I remember telling my mother that, oh, I had gone to Ruleville, Mississippi, to help register Black people to vote for Congress. And my mama said, “Well, I don’t know why you way up there.” Said, “Black people don’t vote here in Bolton.” And so it hit me. And Lord have mercy. In my own hometown, you know, I was in the same situation. And we did voter registration. We did all kind of things.
“For me, having gone through those life experiences and now to see a Scott come along, you know, it not only brings tears to your eye, but it also says that there’s hope.”
We brought Head Start to the community, and started understanding that real freedom comes with political freedom. And so we started holding meetings about what we wanted to do. We decided to run three people for the board and the three African Americans won.
But it really wasn’t a good four years on that term because the current mayor didn’t want any progress. So we ran an all-Black slate: mayor, clerk, alderman. We won every position.
We’re talking about 50 years ago, and all these challenges that you faced, all these challenges to being able to vote, being able to assume office, being able to function as a mayor in a town that is so segregated. Fifty years later, Scott Colom is winning in Mississippi.
I want to ask you to reflect on when you became aware of his candidacy and what you thought about the potential there.
One of the challenges that I’ve had to deal with is that every time I run for public office, I’ve always been the first. But I wanted to create some kind of vehicle to get other people engaged. So we formed the Mississippi Black Leadership Institute. Well, Scott Colom was in the first class. And he really said, “I want to run for something. I don’t know what it is.” He said, “But there’s a district attorney’s position that’s available. It’s three counties.”
We helped Scott put his campaign together. We hooked him up with various people, and he beat a 28-year incumbent as district attorney.
Why do you think he won?
Well, because he had the fire in the belly. And he never met a stranger. And so we prepared him, and he’s one of our star pupils of that class. And look, uh, when the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee would not support him, they—
They would not support him.
They would not support him. But this was my — Bennie Thompson’s position is that Northeasterners were still looking down on Southerners.
Well, did you call them up and scream at Chuck Schumer or somebody and say, “Guys, I am telling you, we got one here who can win?”
Look, we did everything that the system says you should do. We gave the demographics. That district [Colom] represented was not a majority-African American district. He beat that sitting district attorney in a majority-white district because he had a plan and he had a message. We had a rich message, but a poor campaign. Because we couldn’t get our DSCC to help.
Have you called any of those people in national leadership and said, “I told you so?”
Oh yeah. All of a sudden, the week before the election, they’re going to say, “Well, we’re going to be able to do this, but we’re going to shoot the spot and we’ll send it to you.” So you really didn’t give us the money. You know what I’m saying?
So that’s all right. We’re going to keep doing our low budget, social media-attractive thing. And so it took off.
You are 78 years old? Do I have that right?
Yep.
This has been most of your life. The fight for this has been most of your life.
Yep.
You sit here today, we sit here today. Where is your head at in all of this? Did you lock yourself in the bathroom and cry for 10 minutes?
No question. I’m happy for Scott personally. His trajectory is tremendous. But you know, it’s been a tough journey. We had a poll tax put on us that we had to pay money to be a registered voter. We had to interpret sections of the Constitution. In many instances when my mama registered — my mama had a college degree, she was a teacher — but the person who asked her to interpret the Constitution was an elementary school graduate. You see what I’m saying?
I sure do.
And so for me, having gone through those life experiences and now to see a Scott come along, you know, it not only brings tears to your eye, but it also says that there’s hope. There’s hope for young African Americans that at some point, the choice will be, do I stay or leave? It won’t be, “Well, when I get an education, I have to go somewhere else to seek a career.”
And so that’s the exciting part. I’m just really happy. And for a guy who’s been in it over 50 years and been called everything but a child of God, because I’m trying to elevate people who look like me to where I know if they have it, they’ll do a great job. So for Bennie Thompson, Scott’s victory is a dream come true.

- Leave bookings for GTA 6's November 19 release have increased by 32% compared to last year.
- Italy leads with a 91% increase, followed by India at 60% and Ireland at 57%.
- Around 29% of GTA 6 release-day leave bookings cover both Thursday and Friday, creating a four-day weekend.
With just three days remaining until GTA 6 launches on November 19, 2026, employees around the world are already booking time off work. A new report reveals that leave requests for the GTA 6 release date have increased by 32% compared to the same Thursday in 2025. This marks the biggest jump for any working day in 2026 so far, excluding major holiday weeks.
According to global HR platform Remote’s Workforce Intel report, the data comes from full-time employees using its services across multiple countries. Italy recorded the biggest increase in leave bookings at 91%, followed by India at 60%, Ireland at 57%, Spain at 44%, and the United Kingdom at 42%.
The report also reveals how employees are planning their time off around the GTA 6 release. Around 29% of launch-day leave bookings cover both Thursday, November 19, and Friday, November 20, allowing employees to enjoy a four-day break including the weekend.
Meanwhile, 23.7% have booked the entire launch week off, while 17.7% are taking just the release day. The extended breaks could come in handy, as Rockstar North co-head Rob Nelson previously revealed that his GTA 6 playthrough took around 80 hours, including the main story and some optional objectives.
Remote also compared the figures with previous major gaming releases. GTA 6’s 32% increase surpassed Battlefield 6‘s 23% and Hollow Knight: Silksong‘s 16%, making it the biggest launch-day increase among the games examined since 2022.
However, these figures only represent employees on Remote’s platform and do not confirm that everyone taking time off is doing so to play GTA 6. In fact, only one in 170 launch-day leave notes explicitly mentions the game or related terms.
With GTA 6 launching in just three days, employees who haven’t planned their time off can still submit a leave request. Those interested can check our GTA 6 leave application guide, which includes useful tips and a ready-to-use template. Whether the request gets approved, however, depends on their employer.

UK and allies call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza
- Published
The UK, Australia, Canada and Italy have issued a joint statement urging Israel to "allow immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza", where they say the situation on the ground is "dire".
The foreign ministers warn recent floods have brought "further suffering" to the war-torn territory, which recently had its first winter storm.
The statement says 150,000 tents and other vital supplies are being held at the border.
The Israeli military authority which controls the Gaza crossings has said it is co-ordinating with the US-led Board of Peace and the UN on a winter plan, and that 93,000 tents and 8,600 aid trucks with winter supplies had entered the territory.
It added that reconstruction "can only begin after Hamas fully disarms".
The UN Office for the Co-ordination of Humanitarian Affairs said the widespread flooding and a landslide led to a number of deaths, thousands of damaged shelters and the suspension of critical services.
The statement from the British, Australian, Canadian and Italian foreign ministers says, external: "This situation is entirely reversible - and there is still time to act before the winter fully sets in."
"The crossings must be opened, and the tents allowed in. Dual-use items necessary for humanitarian operations and early recovery must be granted entry before it is too late."
The European Union issued a similar statement on Saturday, external, reiterating its "grave concern" over what it called the "persistent and devastating humanitarian crisis".
The EU also urged Israel to comply with international law.
The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Israel responded by launching a military campaign in Gaza, during which more than 74,690 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
Israeli air strikes and other attacks have continued to take place almost every day despite the ceasefire agreed in October last year.

There’s nothing like the feeling of a brand-new planner, and I've found the best planners if you're shopping for something new for 2027. Whether you're looking to get a little more organized or just love having somewhere to write everything down, the beginning of the year is a great time for a fresh start, and most planner companies have their 2027 planner designs already available.
The world of planners might seem simple if you've only browsed your local Target or bookstore to see what planners they might have on hand. But there's a wide world of options out there that can perfectly suit your needs, especially if you're willing to build your own travel notebook or write in the dates on an undated paper planner, or open to trying your first Japanese-style planner.
After years of testing and a constant stack of planners on my desk, I've found these standout favorite planner styles that could benefit everyone. If you're looking for a tech companion to your paper planner, check out my guides to the Best Digital Wall Calendars and Best Digital Notebooks to help keep your calendar and thoughts organized digitally.
Updated November 2026: I've updated the information in this guide to reflect planner availability as 2026 comes to an end and 2027 designs become available. I'm also currently testing 2027 designs from Plum Paper, Laurel Denise, My PA Planner, and Sterling Ink, plus an undated design of Aura Estelle if you're looking for a planner you can start using in December 2026 into the new year.
The Best Planners
If you need a single planner that can do it all and won't burn through your back-to-school budget, this is the one. The Roterunner Purpose Planner is an undated planner that has monthly spreads, weekly spreads, and two full open pages for each week, so there's plenty of room to write longer lists or a project brainstorm. Each monthly and weekly spread has a ton of premade checklist sections for you to use, too. There's even space to track your meals, water intake, and gratitude. It's a planner that actually helps me stay organized and gives me space to track and take notes without running out of room.
The undated nature makes it easy to pick up anytime and use for whichever months you need. Fell off the boat for a few months? No problem. No pages will go to waste when you can fill them in as you go. It only covers six months, but I actually like that; it once again feels like a feasible commitment, especially if you're waffling on how much paper planner you want to promise to use. I love the massive B5 size ($35) since it's finally enough space for me and all my various to-do lists and brainstorms, but there's also a smaller (and cheaper!) A5 ($28) size. It's truly my go-to planner since it has so much space for me to both use the pre-made lists and the open space to actually stay organized and put all my ideas, plans, and notes into one planner. Most others make me feel like I need a companion notebook, but not the Roterunner.
The covers come in a variety of simple colors, and in both hard cover or soft, but the butter-soft faux leather soft cover is my favorite of the bunch. Get it in B5 size if you're always looking for more room in your journals and planners—you won't regret it.
If you're getting into planners, there's no way you won't hear about Hobonichi at some point. There are a few different planners the brand makes, with the Techo being the most popular model. I tested the similar Hobonichi Cousin, which adds weekly spreads to the front of the planner after the monthly overviews. While I don't typically prefer a daily planner style, I was surprised by how much I liked using the Hobonichi. All of Hobonichi's planners use Tomoe River S paper, which is super thin but won't bleed through to the other side. It's also super smooth to the touch and to write on. I liked adding my own structure to the daily pages; I sketched a box to separate my to-do lists and habit trackers from my hourly agenda for the day, and then would usually freeform the rest of the page based on what was on my mind. The Cousin I tested and photographed is an A5 size, while the standard Techo is the smaller A6.
Hobonichi's 2027 editions are here, so you can stock up on your planner for next year right now, plus tons of colors, covers, and other accessories, some of which are unique to 2027. I recommend picking out a protective cover since I did ding up my soft cover quite a bit, and that was just from being used around the house with an occasional trip in a bag. There are little quotes in the corners, but I got a Japanese version instead of an English one, so I can't actually read mine. But honestly, I'm glad I did; I prefer the Japanese lettering to English words on the corners of each page.
I've been obsessed with travel notebooks this year. A travel notebook uses bands to connect three or four notebooks together, and I love using this system to build a customized planner designed for my exact needs. It makes it easy to change the design, too, since you can just switch out a single notebook when it's full.
I really like Cloth & Paper's Travel Notebook Collection. There are 13 different notebooks you can choose from to include in your travel notebook, ranging from classic weekly and monthly spreads to more unique options like a daily wellness notebook and a task planner. It's really a great option if you want a couple of specific things, or even just a regular monthly and weekly notebook plus a blank notebook in the back you can fill with to-do lists and replace anytime without needing an entirely new planner. It's great for students, too, because you can have a notebook dedicated to tracking your assignments and syllabus for the semester. You'll need to create your own, though, as Cloth & Paper doesn't have a dedicated academic notebook for you to select.
I tried both the A5 Slim and the Pocket Plus size, and I really prefer the A5 Slim for a traditional planner experience. The Pocket Plus would be fun to bring on a trip; I wish I'd had it on my latest trip to store little mementos and important things like parking receipts, and could have also written out notes and the plan for the week-long trip. But otherwise, the larger A5 slim was much easier to write on and use for my daily notes and planning.
You'll want the Clear Vinyl Travel Notebook Cover ($23 to $25) no matter which size you choose, which includes elastic bindings to bring all the notebooks you buy together, and you can also pick up more colorful elastic options to add a little more personality to your planner.
I've heard a lot of good things about Erin Condren. Founded in 2005 by Erin Condren, it's known for the LifePlanner that's full of various spreads and productivity tools that you can customize, but there are other variations of planners you can find from the brand. While you'll usually customize your Erin Condren planner if you shop directly on the site, there's a predesigned Target line you can shop that won't give you options, but will give you a well-made planner that's ready to go immediately.
I've been testing the Erin Condren Academic Planner you'll find at Target, but it's sold out as we head into the new year; Erin Condren's website has similar, but more expensive options with more cover and customization options. This base version from Target is a great fit for students and people with deadline-style or client-based work they want to organize. Each month has two pages following the monthly spread to set your most important to-dos and dates, but also a full page to track the month's deadlines and what class (or client, or in my case, story beat) they're for. After that, there are weekly spreads with long columns for each day, and seven blocks of four lines that you can label with things like specific classes, clubs, or organizations, or parenting and household tasks, as I track. It's been a really easy planner to add into my lifestyle, even though it's made for students. There's a class tracker in the front of the planner, too, which I skipped using, plus a detailed holiday calendar, and the back has project and exam pages, plus blank note pages, and even a simple sheet of stickers with things like “Exam,” “Midterm,” and “Paper Due.”
Academic planners usually start in August, so you probably don't want a planner like this if you want something fresh for the new year. But it's still my favorite I've tried if it's your preferred style. Erin Condren does have annual layouts and its popular LifePlanner designs available in 2027 layouts, and other specific designs like budget planners and teacher lesson planners if you're looking for something specific, too.
Honorable Mentions
Like I said, there's a huge world of planners out there. Here are a few that the Reviews team and I at WIRED have tested and enjoyed.
More Planners I’ve Tried
Agendio Basic Planner starting at $48: This is a completely customizable planner. I liked it, and you have the option to design your own pages, and the folder-style cover will protect both the pages and binding. I didn't love the customization tools or abilities as much as I wanted to, and there are a lot of steps to create your planner. I preferred the custom tools of Plum Paper over it. It's a good planner if the pages and binder-style are what you're looking for, and you can find some preset options that usually start around $48 for the smallest page size and black-and-white print.
Ban.do 12-Month Planner for $20: If you're looking for another affordable option but want something with more personality than the Roterunner above, Ban.do's planners are fun and colorful and even come with a page of stickers. It's only a horizontal weekly format, though, which I don't love (but maybe you do!) and the 2027 12-Month designs are now available.
Happy Planner 12-Month Planner for $33: Happy Planner uses disc-bound planners to make it easy to remove and add pages or covers, which is nice for customizability. But they're a very specific aesthetic, and personally, I didn't love turning pages on the discs. Still, it's a good planner if you like the style, and they come in a ton of different layouts. Right now, you can get a Happy Planner that starts in July 2026 and will run you until June 2027, perfect for tracking the academic year.
Laurel Denise Nancy Academic Planner for $44: These planners are cool because you'll look at the month and your weekly at the same time, as the slim weekly pages lay on top of the monthly spread. However, I write way, way too much for the space in these planners, at least for the Nancy design I tested previously. It's great if you just want to write a couple to-dos and meetings per day, but if you want space for detailed lists, you might feel the way I did. I'm currently testing the 2027 Luna ($62) and Scout ($62) planners from Laurel Denise to see if I still feel the same way compared to the original design.
Leuchtturm1917 12-Month Ruled Planner for $29: This is a solid, minimalist planner that has a popular following. It's a simple horizontal weekly layout with the week on one side and a lined page on the other. It's not enough space for everything I write down, but if you're looking for something simple and space for a couple of lists or notes for each week that fit onto a page, it's a good option for you. Leuchtturm1917 also has a nice line of notebooks that look the same from the outside cover, so make sure you actually get the planner.
Muji Undated Weekly Planner for $7: If you want a super simple, super affordable planner, the Muji Undated Weekly is for you. It's just undated weekly horizontal spreads from front to back, even on the paper cover. It's slim, but still more than a year's worth of weeks in it. It's the most minimalist planner I've tried, and though I'm not a fan of horizontal weekly spreads for my planner needs, it's a great cheap option for a lot of people.
Papier Hardcover 2027 Planner for $40: My favorite thing about Papier's planners is how gorgeous the covers are. Papier has a range of beautiful designs you can choose that feel like they belong on a bookshelf rather than just my planner. I tested one of the annual planners, which has the horizontal weekly layout I don't love on any planner (and you can still get that by choosing the mid-year layout for any cover Papier has if you love that style), but the academic one ($29) has a vertical layout that's much more up my alley. Whichever style you like, you can pick. Papier also has softcover academic planners ($32) that use a ring binding, which is easier to lay open than the hard cover binding, and still has both mid-year and academic layout options.
Passion Planner 2027 Planner for $50: This planner was really popular when I was in college, and maybe it still is with the college kids. I liked it, but I feel like the Purpose Planner does a similar thing but better, at least for my needs. It's got vertical spread, but every slot is timed, so I can't use it as a to-do list. It's great for anyone needing to plan out a super detailed schedule and has some to-do list spaces on the bottom, but they're pretty small in my opinion to work for an entire week. It's good for students who only want to track their busy schedules and a couple assignments and tasks for each week.
Some Planner Accessories
Looking for what to pair with your planner? Here are some of our team's favorite daily tools and planner accessories.
Passion Planner Passion Highlighters for $20: If your planner could use a little color, I really like Passion Planner's highlighter sets. They're nice and thin-tipped to fit into slim planner lines, and I especially like the vintage colors for adding color without it feeling neon-bright. You can use the highlighters to organize your plans by type (I like to do red for work, blue for my kid, yellow for things like doctor's appointments, and green for my social life) or color-code your class subjects like we used to do with ringed notebooks.
Pilot Metropolitan Fountain Pen for $34: I never understood the appeal of a fountain pen until I bought one. A properly smoothed fountain pen nib requires very little pressure to write with and seems to glide across the page with a soft, satisfying scratching sound. I know, I'm one of those people now. Much of my initial skepticism came from the perceived complexity of caring for and using a fountain pen, which is very much overblown. My favorite pen of the dozen I've tested is the Pilot Metropolitan with the fine nib. It's easy to work with, taking either prefilled ink cartridges, which you can pop in and out without ever spilling any ink, or you can fill it yourself using a converter and the ink of your choice. I started off using the cartridges, but eventually my quest for a waterproof ink led me to the converter and this sketching ink. Once a week or so, I dip the Metropolitan nib in the bottle of ink and twist the converter to fill the chamber with ink—that's all there is to it. Whichever fountain pen you find works best for you, you’ll find you'll have a quite simply better writing experience. —Scott Gilbertson
Plum Paper Seasonal Stickers for $10: There are a lot of stickers out there you could use for your planners, but my favorites—especially for the holidays—are from Plum Paper. They're beautiful and fun, and are mostly nice and small to fit into small lines or monthly charts without eating up the entire section. I like that there's a mix of shapes and styles, and you can also shop stickers for themes like home, fitness, wellness, and baby milestones. You can even make your own custom stickers (starting at $12), which are only thick line-style stickers where you can customize the word and icon on them. Still, very handy!
Planner Alternatives
Not everyone needs or wants a rigid planner. If you just need daily to-do lists or are a fan of bullet journals, consider getting a great notebook instead.
Maybe you just want a plain, lined notebook. One of our former reviewers recommended the Midori MD Notebook, and I found it to be a nice small size if you're looking for something minimal. It comes in lined, unlined, or dot-grid, and uses paper made from cotton pulp (just like money!) Midori’s notebooks are designed to fit inside notebook or journal covers (which you can find all over Etsy). The pages are a subtle off-white and have a weight and texture that draw you in.
One of our reviewers skips a planner entirely and instead writes down his to-do list on a 3-by-5 index card. He puts that index card into his pocket with a pocket-sized memo book like this one from Field Notes ($13 for three), where he jots down notes throughout the day to use for the next day's to-do list. Both the notebook and index cards fit inside a waxed canvas notebook cover to keep them safe from the elements (or just his pocket). It's an affordable and easy-to-manage system.
FAQs
Why Choose a Paper Planner?
Studies show that it's good for your brain to write things down. Sure, you could put your calendar in an online tool, but putting pen to paper activates more brain connectivity. We're more likely to remember and learn things if we write them down by hand, so using a paper planner for your to-do list can make it easier to remember. Plus, it's fun! You're given a creative space to let out everything you need to remember, from appointments to the day's tasks, and customize it in a way that best helps you stay organized.
What Style Paper Planner Is Best for You?
Paper planners mainly come in two styles: weekly and daily. Daily planners have an entire page dedicated to each day, while weekly planners have an entire week spread across just two pages. These aren't the only options (monthly is another popular one, for example, but not as popular as these two styles), but they're the most common you'll see. I like daily planners for folks who have a really busy schedule they want to plan out, and long daily to-do lists. Weekly planners are great if you want to be able to write down a few things per day but don't need an entire page.
What Sizes Do Planners Come In?
Here are a couple common planner sizes. My favorite are the larger sizes since I like lots of room to doodle, but the smaller A5 is a popular choice for a book-sized planner that won't take up too much space. Not all paper planners use the same sizing names—Moleskine, for example, calls its A5 size a large—so you'll want to check measurements before you purchase.
- A5 (5.8 by 8.3 inches)
- Regular/Medium / B5 (7 by 9 inches)
- Large/Letter (8.5 by 11 inches)
- Personal/Pocket (3.5 by 5.5 inches)

Journalist’s Arrest Adds to Fears Israeli Security Agency Is Being Politicized
Abed Abu Shehadeh, a Palestinian citizen of Israel, was detained without being charged with a crime, raising concerns that the domestic security service is overstepping its authority.
Abed Abu Shehadeh, a 38-year-old journalist and a Palestinian citizen of Israel, said he was putting on his pajamas on the evening of Nov. 3 when police officers and intelligence agents burst into his family’s third-floor apartment in Jaffa.
They strip-searched him, confiscated his phone, allowed him to dress and then whisked him away, he said in an interview at a restaurant in the city.
Five days later, after interrogations by Israel’s domestic security agency, the Shin Bet, Mr. Abu Shehadeh, who lives with his wife and two young children, was let go.
A former elected member of the Tel Aviv-Jaffa City Council, Mr. Abu Shehadeh has not been charged with a crime. The Israeli authorities have not publicly offered a reason for his arrest, though court records reviewed by The New York Times show that he was accused of being in contact with an unnamed “foreign agent.”
His highly publicized arrest — a week after Israel’s national elections — came as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies have claimed that foreign actors illegally funneled large amounts of money to bribe Arab citizens to vote for Arab political parties.
Critics say that Mr. Netanyahu and his allies are seeking to undermine the legitimacy of the record gains by Arab parties in the Parliament, or the Knesset, by contending without basis that Arab voters stole the election.

Maharashtra extends 7% VAT on aviation turbine fuel till April 14
On May 14, the state government had reduced the VAT on ATF from 18% to 7% for six months, with effect from May 15.
The Maharashtra government has extended the concessional 7% value-added tax (VAT) on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) it announced in May by five months, until April 14, 2027, allowing airlines to continue paying the lower rate.
In a notification dated November 12, the state finance department extended the existing tax concession, which was due to expire on November 14. The tax cut earlier this year came after global crude oil prices rose and the West Asia conflict disrupted airline operations, pushing up carriers’ operating costs.
"Whereas, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 9 of the Maharashtra Value Added Tax Act, 2002 (Mah, IX of 2005), the Government of Maharashtra has, vide Government Notification, Finance Department No. MVAT. 2026/C.R. 28 /Taxation -1, Dated the 14th May 2026, amended the SCHEDULE 'B' appended to the said Act and has reduced the rate of tax on the Aviation Turbine Fuel (Duty paid) to seven per cent. for the period commencing from the 15th May 2026 and ending on the 14th November 2026," the notification said.
"..And whereas, the Government considers it expedient to extend the said rate of tax on the Aviation Turbine Fuel (Duty paid) till the 14th April 2027," it added.
On May 14, the state government had reduced the VAT on ATF from 18% to 7% for six months, with effect from May 15. The earlier tax structure included an 18% levy at Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and Pune airports.
ATF is among the largest expenses for airlines, accounting for around 40-50% of their total operating costs.
To be sure, reducing fuel taxes helps ease some of the cost pressure on airlines, although the extent of the benefit depends on various operating expenses.

Former Indian cricketer Sachin Tendulkar has joined the cap table of Hyderabad-based cleantech startup Recykal. The startup did not disclose the size of the investment. In a statement, Recykal said that Tendulkar infused the capital during the extension of the startup’s recently closed $23 Mn bridge round. Back in June, the clean tech startup had raised $17.6 Mn in equity funding. The round also comprised an additional secondary component worth $5.4 Mn, which saw participation from existing backers and family offices. “What drew me to Recykal was seeing how technology was being used to solve an everyday problem. Recykal’s mission to use technology to drive behavioural change across 1 Bn people is what really connected with me, and I hope together we can encourage more people to make responsible choices every day,” said Tendulkar in a statement. Founded in 2016 by Abhay Deshpande, Abhishek Deshpande, Ekta Narain, Vikram Prabakar and Anirudha Jalan, Recykal operates a B2B marketplace for recyclable materials. It also provides software solutions to help brands track plastic and e-waste recycling to meet compliance mandates. The startup also recently launched a deposit return system (DRS), a reverse vending machine service for recovering consumer packaging. Under DRS, consumers pay a refundable deposit on containers at purchase and get it back when they return the container to a collection point. Backed by the likes of Morgan Stanley, 360 ONE, Circulate Capital and the Murugappa Group, the startup has raised more than $60 Mn in funding to date. Recykal claims to operate a network of more than 5,000 waste aggregators and recyclers and claims to cater to 650 enterprise brands, including the likes of Hindustan Unilever, Samsung and BMW. In June this year, the startup had told Inc42 that it closed FY26 with a gross revenue of ₹1,498 Cr, up 53.2% from ₹978 Cr in the year ago fiscal. However, losses jumped 7% to ₹60 Cr compared to ₹56 Cr in FY25. Interestingly, Tendulkar’s investment in Recykal comes almost two weeks after he backed gaming startup Metasports Interactive, the company behind mobile cricket strategy game Hitwicket. Besides, the retired cricket icon has also invested in a range of other startups such as used car marketplace Spinny, listed fintech startup Kissht, and former Swiggy Instamart leader Karthik Gurumurthy’s activewear brand Ten X You.

After Decades of Blood and Mistrust, Doubts Over Who’s to Blame for an Israeli Hostage
Israeli spies kidnapped and killed Iranians. They were convinced that Tehran was to blame for a fallen airman. Alternative theories got little attention, until now.
Gen. Abdullah Saberi, an Iranian commander, stepped out for a jog early one morning in an upscale diplomatic quarter of Syria’s capital. Israeli intelligence officers waited nearby. Posing as movers, they had slipped past the neighborhood’s security checkpoints.
As he headed for a nearby park, General Saberi passed two men who carried an oversize refrigerator box. In a flash, the men restrained the general, drugged him, threw the box over his head, shoved him into a white van and left as if nothing had happened.
He was whisked to Israel for interrogation, according to numerous officials in the Middle East, including senior Iranian officials close to General Saberi and a Syrian official who reviewed video of the September 2021 kidnapping.
As a veteran of Iran’s powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, General Saberi knew many secrets. But his interrogators were interested in only one.
What did he know about Ron Arad?
Mr. Arad, an Israeli airman, vanished decades ago, and the Israeli military says he is the only service member classified as missing in action. The government’s long search for him has captivated the public and has come to symbolize Israel’s commitment, rooted in Jewish tradition, to bringing its soldiers home, dead or alive. Articles, books and documentaries have been produced about the hunt for Mr. Arad.
The Israeli government was so determined to find him that, even four decades after his disappearance, it took the risk of kidnapping General Saberi in the shadow of his own embassy.
